summary.intent: Backfill missing Phase 47 summaries and Phase 48 verification, implement the share itemName lazy-backfill API endpoint + web wiring to close an open REQ-4 gap, then ship the feature branch as a PR.
summary.outcome: All three bookkeeping tasks completed and committed on branch `feat/share-itemname-lazy-backfill` (171 API tests + 48 web tests green, TypeScript clean, STATE.md advanced to 100%). Ship workflow blocked at push: commits were made without 1Password SSH signatures and the Bash sandbox cannot reach the signer to re-sign them.

repo: Phase 47 shipped via PR #494 but SUMMARY.md files were never written to disk, causing the GSD resume-incomplete invariant to fire as a false positive on every subsequent `/gsd-progress --next` run.

Commit signing is enforced via 1Password SSH: `commit.gpgsign=true`, `gpg.format=ssh`, `gpg.ssh.program=op-ssh-sign`. The Bash sandbox cannot reach the 1Password agent, so commits made inside the sandbox are silently unsigned.

The pre-commit hook `check-api-client.sh` requires `pnpm api:generate` to be run and committed any time a new API endpoint is added; generated files carry an OpenAPI spec version bump (0.38.0 → 0.39.0) in every file header as normal regeneration noise.

The codebase convention for sharer-only guards is explicit inline `if (share.createdByUserId !== userId) throw new ForbiddenException()` per service method — not a shared helper. Six existing methods all follow this pattern; a helper used by only 2 of 6 would be less consistent.
Single-field PATCH endpoints are the established convention: `/encrypted-key`, `/permission`, `/hide`, now `/item-name`. Each gets its own DTO, service method, and controller handler.
`.planning/intel/` contains pre-existing untracked files that predate this session and should not be committed as part of feature work.

code.finding: `void itemNameEncrypted` was a deliberate no-op stub left in `backfillSentShareItemNames` pending the PATCH endpoint; the backfill pass in `fetchAllSentShares` was also commented out waiting for the same endpoint.
New DTO mirroring `UpdateEncryptedKeyDto`: single `@IsString() @IsHexadecimal()` field `itemNameEncrypted`. The server stores the client ciphertext as-is and never re-encrypts.

`updateShareItemName` is a structural copy of `updateShareEncryptedKey` — same ownership guard, same `prisma.share.update` call, different field name. Two methods sharing this shape is within convention; a helper is warranted only if a third emerges.
Regenerated function is `sharesControllerUpdateShareItemName` — the naming convention is `sharesController` + PascalCase HTTP verb + route segments. This is the symbol to import on the web side.

workflow: The GSD resume-incomplete invariant (`plans.length > summaries.length`) has no awareness of whether a phase actually shipped via a PR; it will false-positive whenever SUMMARY.md files are omitted even after code merges. Manual override requires either writing the missing summaries or passing `--no-resume`.

Commits made inside the Claude Code Bash sandbox cannot be signed with 1Password SSH; `git rebase --force-rebase` and explicit `-S` flags do not help when the agent (`op-ssh-sign`) is unreachable. Re-signing requires running `git rebase -i` from a terminal with 1Password unlocked.

Running 4 cleanup agents in parallel (reuse / simplification / efficiency / altitude) converged on the same finding (service-guard duplication), giving high confidence the code was already clean without needing a fifth pass.

When `pnpm api:generate` updates every generated file's header version, the resulting diff is large but semantically trivial — it should be committed as part of the feature commit, not separately, to keep the hook happy.

friction: GSD false-positive resume gate: Phase 47 had 5 plans / 0 summaries on disk despite code being fully merged, causing `--next` to route to `/gsd-execute-phase 47` (which would have re-run already-merged refactors). Required manual investigation of git history to identify and override.

Bash sandbox cannot access 1Password SSH signer: all 3 commits on the feature branch are unsigned, blocking the ship workflow at `git push` (the PR signature gate would reject them). `git rebase --force-rebase` and `-S` flag had no effect.
api:generate produces a large diff (version bump in every generated file header) even when adding a single endpoint, making it harder to spot the actual generated change in code review.
open_items: Ship the feature branch: the 3 commits on `feat/share-itemname-lazy-backfill` must be re-signed from a terminal with 1Password unlocked (`git rebase -i HEAD~3`, re-commit each with signing enabled), then pushed and PR'd.
Run `/gsd-complete-milestone` to formally close v1.1 once the PR merges — STATE.md is at 100% but the milestone archive step hasn't run.
Phase 48 live-environment human checks are still pending: web-e2e smoke test and a two-party UAT (sharer + recipient) to confirm the itemName backfill round-trips correctly in production.
`.planning/intel/` contains untracked pre-existing files; ownership and whether they should be committed or gitignored is unresolved.
